cohort: The study included 96 patients who received either intrauterine balloon tamponade (IUBT) or compression sutures for major postpartum hemorrhage (>1000 ml) between 2014 and 2018 at a single obstetric unit.
finding: Intrauterine balloon tamponade (IUBT) and compression sutures had similarly high overall success rates in controlling major postpartum hemorrhage, though IUBT performed better in cases of placenta praevia.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery was a distinguishing patient characteristic, with more vaginal deliveries observed in the IUBT group compared to the compression sutures group.
